objectives: Quantify the sixth mass extinction + biodiversity loss.
Survey climate-change ecology + range + phenology shifts.
Map the AI + eDNA + planetary-boundary frontier.

slides.title: Extinction crisis + sixth mass extinction
slides.body:
**Background extinction rate**: ~0.1-1 species per million per year (E/MSY) from fossil record (Pimm + Raven 2014). **Current rate**: ~100-1000× background — comparable to the five known mass extinctions of the geological record. **Ceballos + Ehrlich 2015** *Science Advances*; Ceballos 2017 *PNAS*: 'the biological annihilation' — quantified the sixth mass extinction as already underway.

**Drivers (acronym HIPPO)** (E. O. Wilson):
- **H**abitat loss + degradation (largest single driver — ~50% of vertebrate declines).
- **I**nvasive species (esp. on islands).
- **P**ollution (chemical, nutrient, plastic, noise, light).
- **P**opulation growth + consumption.
- **O**verexploitation (hunting, fishing, wildlife trade).
Add **climate change** + **disease** as growing.

**IUCN Red List**: global authority on species threat status. Categories: Extinct (EX), Extinct in Wild (EW), Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN), Vulnerable (VU), Near Threatened (NT), Least Concern (LC), Data Deficient (DD), Not Evaluated (NE). 2024: ~46,000 of ~163,000 assessed species threatened. ~28% of mammals, ~13% of birds, ~41% of amphibians, ~37% of sharks + rays, ~21% of reptiles, ~38% of trees.

**IPBES 2019 Global Assessment**: ~1 million species at risk of extinction — most ever assessed at scale.

**Living Planet Index** (WWF + ZSL): index of vertebrate population abundance from monitored populations. 2024 report: **73% decline since 1970** (4391 monitored species, ~35000 populations). Geographic: Latin America/Caribbean –95%, Africa –76%, Asia-Pacific –60%, Europe –35% (Europe earlier-impacted; recent stabilization). Freshwater species –85%; marine –56%; terrestrial –69%.

**Extinction debt** (Tilman 1994; Kuussaari 2009): lag between habitat loss + actual extinction; many extinctions are 'committed' but not yet realized. Conversely, **immigration credit** for habitat restoration.

**Defaunation** (Dirzo 2014 *Science*): widespread loss of individuals + populations even before species extinction. Average ~25% decline in vertebrate populations across monitored species.

**De-extinction**: emerging proposals to revive extinct species via cloning + genome editing.
- **Mammoth project** (Colossal Biosciences): using elephant cells + CRISPR to engineer cold-adapted Asian elephants approximating *Mammuthus*; targeted for Pleistocene Park (Zimov, Siberia) ecosystem-restoration.
- **Thylacine** (Pask + Colossal).
- **Passenger pigeon** (Revive + Restore; Ben Novak).
Controversies: ethics, ecological risk, opportunity costs, replacement vs revival. Pleistocene Park rewilding hypothesis: large herbivores compact snow + maintain steppe-tundra grasslands which sequester carbon + slow permafrost thaw.

**Key recent extinctions**: golden toad (1989), Western black rhino (2011), Baiji Yangtze dolphin (~2007), Bramble Cay melomys (2016 — first mammal extinction attributed to climate change), Pinta Island tortoise (Lonesome George 2012). Many more await formal declaration.

slides.title: Climate-change ecology: phenology + ranges + thermal mismatch
slides.body:
**Climate change** is restructuring ecosystems globally — observed responses already pervasive (Parmesan + Yohe 2003 *Nature* — 'a globally coherent fingerprint'; **Camille Parmesan** + IPCC AR4-AR6).

**Phenology shifts**: timing of biological events (flowering, leaf-out, migration, hatching) advancing at ~2-5 days/decade across thousands of species. **Spring advancement** > autumn delay. UK phenological records (Marsham, Lyon, Sparks); North American USA-NPN + lilac records; European MAERI.

**Phenological mismatch**: predator-prey, plant-pollinator, host-parasite timing may decouple under unequal rates of response. **Both 2009 *Nature*** Pied flycatcher caterpillar mismatch; Visser + Both 2005. May drive demographic decline + extirpation.

**Range shifts** (Parmesan + Yohe 2003; Chen 2011 *Science*): species moving poleward (~17 km/decade) + upslope (~11 m/decade) on average — though variable + lagging behind isotherm velocity. Leading-edge expansion + trailing-edge contraction. Marine species shifting 4× faster than terrestrial (Pinsky 2013) — ocean velocity higher.

**Climate velocity** (Loarie 2009): rate at which a climate zone moves across landscape (km/yr). Tropical lowlands face high velocity — nowhere to move to. Mountains face altitudinal escape but cap out at summits ('mountaintop extinction').

**Thermal mismatch + tolerance** (Tewksbury 2008): tropical ectotherms live closer to their thermal optimum — small warming can push them off the warm side. Tropical species + low-latitude marine ectotherms most vulnerable per °C.

**Tropicalization** (Vergés 2014 + Wernberg 2016 *Science*): warming + tropical species expansion into temperate zones; canopy loss + regime shifts (kelp forest → urchin barrens; coral takeover of temperate reefs).

**Ocean warming + marine heatwaves**: ~90% of trapped greenhouse heat absorbed by oceans (Cheng 2024). Marine heatwaves (MHWs) — discrete extreme warm events lasting days to months. 2014-16 'Blob' in NE Pacific killed seabirds + altered fisheries; 2016 Great Barrier Reef bleaching; 2023 N Atlantic + Mediterranean MHW.

**Ocean acidification**: pCO₂ uptake → carbonate chemistry shift; –0.1 pH unit since 1750; affects calcifiers (corals, pteropods, mollusks). See P42.

**Deoxygenation**: warm + stratified ocean holds less O₂; expansion of oxygen minimum zones (OMZ) (Schmidtko 2017 *Nature*; Breitburg 2018 *Science*).

**Tipping points + planetary boundaries** (Rockström 2009 *Nature*; Steffen 2015 *Science*; Lenton 2008 *PNAS*): Earth-system thresholds beyond which feedbacks lock in catastrophic shifts. Examples: Amazon dieback, West Antarctic ice-sheet collapse, AMOC slowdown, coral reef collapse, boreal forest dieback, permafrost-carbon release. Planetary-boundary framework: 9 dimensions (climate, biodiversity, N + P cycles, land system, freshwater, ocean acidification, atmospheric aerosols, ozone, novel entities); 6 currently transgressed (2023 update).

**Disease emergence + zoonoses**: habitat encroachment + biodiversity loss + climate increase zoonotic spillover risk. **Ebola, SARS, COVID-19, Nipah, monkeypox**. **EcoHealth + One Health** framework.

slides.title: Conservation frontier: eDNA + AI + restoration + rewilding + 30×30
slides.body:
**Environmental DNA (eDNA)** (Ficetola 2008; Bohmann + Taberlet 2014): detect species from filtered water, soil, or air via PCR + sequencing of organism-shed DNA. **Metabarcoding** uses universal primers (12S rRNA for fish; COI for invertebrates; ITS for fungi) to inventory whole communities. Revolutionary for biodiversity surveys, rare-species detection, invasive-species early warning, and microbial-eukaryotic diversity. Programs: ARMS, NOAA eDNA Atlas, ECOMOL, Eurofish, TARA Oceans.

**Camera traps + AI**: motion-triggered cameras deployed globally. **Wildlife Insights** (Google + WWF + Conservation International + Smithsonian + WCS + ZSL + NPS): cloud platform for camera-trap images; AI species ID for 1000+ species; analyzed >50M images. **Snapshot Serengeti** + **Snapshot Safari**: citizen-science + AI. **MegaDetector** open-source. **eBird** (Cornell Lab) for bird sightings — >1B observations.

**Bioacoustics + AI**: passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) of birds, bats, cetaceans, frogs, insects. **BirdNET** (Cornell) deep-learning ID. **Rainforest Connection** uses old cellphones + AI to detect chainsaws + gunshots + poaching. **HappyWhale** photo-ID of cetaceans (humpback whale, blue whale).

**Remote sensing + Earth observation**: LANDSAT (1972+), Sentinel-2, PlanetScope (high-frequency 3-m), Sentinel-3 for ocean color, ICESat-2 for canopy height, NISAR (2025+) for biomass + L-band SAR. **Google Earth Engine** + **Planet Labs** + **Microsoft Planetary Computer** democratized petabyte-scale EO analysis.

**Machine learning for ecology** (Christin 2019; Tuia 2022 *Nat Commun*): species distribution models (random forests, BRT, MaxEnt, deep learning), automated counting (Sonnentag et al.), trait imputation, ecological forecasting. **Foundation models** emerging (Bio-ESM, Bird-CLEF). Wildlife Insights + PrismaticAI + iNaturalist computer-vision pipelines. **AI is reshaping monitoring** + creating decision-relevant biodiversity intelligence.

**Restoration ecology** (SER + Suding 2015): reassembling ecosystems after disturbance. Levels: ecological rehabilitation, restoration, replacement. **UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration 2021-2030**. Examples: prairie reconstruction, forest replanting, coral restoration (gene-bank + assisted gene flow + microfragmentation), kelp restoration, wetland creation, river daylighting + dam removal (Klamath 2024 largest in US history).

**Rewilding** (Soulé + Noss 1998; Carver 2021; Perino 2019 *Science*): restoration through reintroduction of large herbivores + apex predators, removal of anthropogenic barriers, allowing self-organization. **Knepp Estate** (UK, Tree 2018) + **Oostvaardersplassen** (Netherlands, controversial) + **Yellowstone** (wolves + grizzlies + bison) + **Pleistocene Park** (Siberia, mammoth-steppe) + **Iberian lynx + Tauros** (Europe). Approaches contested but mainstreaming.

**Planetary boundaries** (Rockström 2009; Steffen 2015): 9-dimension safe-operating-space framework. 6 of 9 currently transgressed (2023 update — Richardson 2023). Includes biosphere integrity, biogeochemical flows (N + P), land system change, novel entities, climate. Influence on EU Green Deal + global biodiversity framework.

**Nature-based Solutions (NbS)** (IUCN 2016): actions to protect, manage, + restore natural ecosystems that address societal challenges while benefiting biodiversity. Climate adaptation + mitigation, water security, food security, disaster risk, health. Forest carbon, coastal mangroves, urban greenspace.

**Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) 2022** — '30×30' target: protect 30% of land + sea by 2030 + restore 30% of degraded ecosystems. Including indigenous + community-conserved areas + functional connectivity + equitable benefit-sharing. Now embedded in many national strategies.

**Indigenous + community conservation**: ~80% of remaining biodiversity is on lands managed by indigenous peoples (RRI). Biocultural conservation + co-management + IPLC rights central to 30×30 + post-2020 framework.

question.question: Estimate the magnitude of the sixth mass extinction
question.goal: Quantify current extinction rate + compare with background.

steps.reveal: Background rate ~0.1-1 species extinctions per million species per year (E/MSY) from the fossil record. Recent estimates converge ~0.1/MSY for mammals (Pimm + Raven 2014; De Vos 2015).

steps.prompt: How many vertebrate species are documented as extinct since 1500 (~5000 mammals + similar amounts of birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish)?
steps.reveal: IUCN documents ~900 EX/EW species since 1500, dominated by birds (~160), mammals (~80), amphibians (~35), fish (~80), invertebrates (~370+). Many likely extinctions are undocumented (cryptic, microbial, plant) — actual extinctions exceed documented count by 2-100×.

steps.prompt: Per Ceballos + Ehrlich 2015, current rate is ~?× background.
steps.reveal: Ceballos + Ehrlich (2015) compute modern rate at ~100-1000× background depending on taxon + conservative assumptions; for vertebrates ~114× even using conservative '2 E/MSY' background. Comparable to the rate during the 5 known mass extinctions. With current trajectories, IPBES (2019) projects ~1M species at risk.

steps.prompt: Living Planet Index reports vertebrate population decline since 1970?
steps.reveal: Living Planet Index 2024: ~73% decline in monitored vertebrate populations since 1970 (4391 species, ~35000 populations). Highest in Latin America/Caribbean (-95%) + Africa (-76%). Population-level decline (defaunation; Dirzo 2014) precedes + exceeds species extinction — biological annihilation is already underway.

question.question: Why is the AI + eDNA + camera-trap revolution transforming conservation ecology?
options: Conservation ecology historically faced a monitoring bottleneck: knowing what species lived where + how populations were trending required expensive, expert-intensive surveys covering tiny fractions of the planet. AI + eDNA + camera traps + bioacoustics + remote sensing collectively transformed this: (1) eDNA (Ficetola 2008) detects species from filtered water/soil/air via metabarcoding — orders of magnitude cheaper than traditional surveys; (2) Wildlife Insights (Google + WCS + WWF + CI) handles 50M+ camera-trap images with AI species ID at >90% accuracy; (3) BirdNET + bioacoustic ML identify songs + calls at scale; (4) iNaturalist + eBird crowdsourced 1B+ observations; (5) Sentinel + Landsat + Planet provide near-real-time habitat-change detection; (6) ML species distribution models predict ranges + restoration outcomes. Together they yield petabyte-scale biodiversity intelligence enabling planetary-scale conservation + 30×30 monitoring.
question.explanation: AI + eDNA + camera traps + bioacoustics + remote sensing replace expensive human-expert surveys with petabyte-scale biodiversity intelligence — making planetary-scale monitoring + 30×30 conservation feasible.

slides.workedSolution: AI (Wildlife Insights, BirdNET, MegaDetector) + eDNA metabarcoding + camera traps + bioacoustics + Sentinel/Landsat remote sensing + iNaturalist/eBird citizen science collectively eliminate the monitoring bottleneck. Conservation now has petabyte-scale biodiversity intelligence at planetary scale — foundation for 30×30 + global biodiversity framework.

question.question: Designing a climate-smart 30×30 portfolio
question.prompt: A national government must select 30% of its terrestrial area for protection under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. What ecological + climate-change + connectivity + indigenous-rights principles would shape your portfolio, and which monitoring technologies would verify outcomes?

question.question: Mean range shift for European butterflies in northern Europe is ~17 km/decade (Parmesan). At this rate, how many km will a species' range edge shift over 50 years?
question.hint: 17 km/decade × 5 decades = 85 km. Compare with climate velocity in lowland tropical regions (~100-200 km/decade isotherm shift) — many species cannot disperse fast enough → range contraction + extinction risk.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why the ecologist's frontier is now planetary + technological.
question.rubric: Mentions: sixth mass extinction (Ceballos + Ehrlich 2015; IPBES 2019) — ~100-1000× background extinction rates + ~1M species at risk; Living Planet Index -73% since 1970; defaunation (Dirzo). Climate-change ecology: Parmesan + Yohe (2003) globally coherent fingerprint — phenology shifts + range shifts (~17 km/decade poleward, ~11 m/decade upslope) + tropicalization + thermal mismatch + marine heatwaves. Tipping points + planetary boundaries (Rockström 2009; Steffen 2015) — 6 of 9 transgressed. Technological frontier: eDNA + camera traps + bioacoustics + AI (Wildlife Insights, BirdNET) + remote sensing + citizen science (iNaturalist, eBird) eliminate monitoring bottleneck. Restoration ecology + rewilding + de-extinction (Pleistocene Park, woolly mammoth) emerging tools. 30×30 + Kunming-Montreal GBF + nature-based solutions + indigenous + community conservation frame the policy agenda. Ecologists now operate at planetary scale with AI-augmented intelligence — the discipline has become a foundational Anthropocene science.
